newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Thailand looks to South Asia for trade, investment.
newsitem.headline: Thailand looks to South Asia for trade, investment.

text.p: Thailand's Deputy Foreign Minister, Pitak Intrawityanunt, said on Monday Bangkok was keen to boost economic ties with its western South Asia neighbours Bangladesh, India and Sri Lanka.
"In fact, our government is pursuing the policy of 'Look West'. This is a very important region for trade and investment," Intrawityanunt told Reuters in Dhaka.

"It's a big market combine. Huge population, huge natural resources and huge potential," said the minister who arrived on Sunday for a four-day official visit to Bangladesh. He is accompanied by senior officials and a large team of Thai entrepreneurs.
"Unfortunately, we could not put due attention to this region because of frequent changes in government (in Bangkok). But we think it's not too late," Intrawityanunt said.
India, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka have a combined population of more than one billion people.
The minister said Bangkok was particularly keen to boost trade and investment ties with Bangladesh, the country he termed the "gateway to this (South Asia) region".
Intrawityanunt said Bangladesh and Thailand wanted to lift two-way trade, which heavily favours Thailand, from $124 million a year in 1996 to at least $400 million by the year 2000.
Thailand exported goods worth $105 million in 1996.

One Bangladesh official said the Thai effort could be hindered by Thai moves to tighten visa procedures for visitors from some SAARC (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation) countries, including Bangladesh.
The restriction followed complaints from Malaysia that illegal immigrants from South Asia use Bangkok as a corridor.
Press reports in Dhaka recently said some 50,000 Bangladeshis, looking to Malaysia for jobs, were in Thai jungles bordering Malaysia.
The minister said, however, there were only a "few thousand" illegal Bangladeshis in Thai territory. Of them, he said, about 1,000 were awaiting deportation.
The minister said Thailand was eager to relocate labour-intensive industries to Bangladesh which had abundant cheap labour.
About 13 Thai companies had already invested $25 million in Bangladesh, he said.
Yussuf Abdullah Harun, president of the Federation of Bangladesh Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FBCCI) proposed a private export zone for Thailand in Bangladesh.
"We have already developed a private export zone for Korea and another for Japan is underway," he said.

"Pisciculture, textile, leather and footwear, poultry, tourism, horticulture, light engineering and pharmaceuticals are the very attractive areas where Thailand can invest," Harun told a meeting with the business delegation accompanying Intrawityanunt.
Intrawityanunt said: "We are taking note of the opportunities. This visit is the beginning only."
In talks during the past two days, officials and entrepreneurs had agreed to joint ventures in a range of sectors including textiles, poultry, fisheries, construction and energy.
Intrawityanunt, who took office four months ago, has already visited Sri Lanka and plans to visit India next month.
